title: Move Zeroes
prompt:
Write a function in `solution.ts` that moves all zeroes to the end of an array **in place**, preserving the relative order of non-zero elements.

**Approach -- Two-Pointer Swap:**
Maintain a `write` pointer starting at index 0. Iterate through the array with a `read` pointer using a `for` loop. Whenever `nums[read]` is non-zero, swap `nums[write]` and `nums[read]`, then advance `write`. After the loop, all non-zero elements are packed to the front and zeroes fill the remaining positions.

**Requirements:**
1. `export function moveZeroes(nums: number[]): void` -- takes an array of numbers, moves all zeroes to the end in place, and returns nothing
2. Use a `for` loop to iterate through the array
3. Modify the array in place -- do not create a new array

**Examples:**
```typescript
const nums = [0, 1, 0, 3, 12];
moveZeroes(nums);
console.log(nums); // [1, 3, 12, 0, 0]

const single = [0];
moveZeroes(single);
console.log(single); // [0]
```

**Complexity:**
- Time: O(n) -- single pass through the array
- Space: O(1) -- in-place swaps, no extra storage
hints: Keep a write pointer that tracks where the next non-zero element should go
Iterate with a read pointer; when you find a non-zero, swap it to the write position
After swapping, advance the write pointer by one
Swapping instead of overwriting naturally fills the tail with zeroes

solution.ts.name: moveZeroes
solution.ts.description: Export moveZeroes as a named export
Use a for loop to iterate through the array
